rows.grounds: possessive pronoun referring to the subject

items.question: How is the fifteenth ground related to the three powers?
premises: The fifteenth ground has its own nature.
Three powers of the Lord were described before.
items.inference: The fifteenth ground is explained through the three previously described powers.
uncertainties: Exact referent of svaṃ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Its own nature is the fifteenth; that ground is fifteenth-natured, for the three powers of the Lord were described before.

items.question: How are the three powers arranged among knower, knowing, and known?
premises: Those powers are established in threefold form.
The supreme part is knower-form here.
items.inference: The powers are distributed across knower, knowing, and known, with the supreme part as knower.
uncertainties: The exact scope of mātṛmāmeya is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Those very powers are established in the threefold form of knower, knowing, and known; the supreme part is knower-form here, and the instrument part is intermediate.

items.question: What is the nature of the ground in relation to known and power?
premises: The power-holder part and power are its own nature.
There the ground's nature stands separately as inert.
items.inference: The ground's nature is distinguished as separately standing and inert.
uncertainties: Compound boundaries in bhūmeryatpṛthagjaḍamavasthitam are ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The known is supreme; the power-holder part and power are its own nature; thus there the nature of the ground is that which stands separately as inert.

items.question: How is knowability produced by knowers and conditions?
premises: Conditions beginning with knower and knowing do not produce stain.
Knowers range from sakala to Shiva.
Its knowability is by those knowers.
items.inference: Knowability arises through knowers and conditions without produced stain.
uncertainties: The long compound has multiple possible segmentations.
items.plain_english: By conditions beginning with knower and knowing, not produced by stain; but by knowers from sakala to Shiva, its knowability is that which...

items.question: How are the seven divisions related to power-holders?
premises: There are seven divisions of those.
They range from sakala to Shiva.
items.inference: Seven divisions arise among power-holders from sakala to Shiva.
uncertainties: The exact force of udracita is interpretive.
items.plain_english: By power-holders with unmanifest powers, seven divisions of those; from sakala to Shiva, in powers with raised self.

items.question: How do knowability-born divisions make fourteen?
premises: The instrument part of sakala is vidya-kala-natured.
items.inference: The seven knowability-born divisions combine with prior divisions to make fourteen.
uncertainties: The arithmetic relation to verse 7 is inferred.
items.plain_english: Knowability-born seven divisions; thus fourteen; of sakala, the instrument part which is vidya-kala-natured.
